reason: H0 exercises many ares_parse_*_reply APIs but never calls the newly exposed ares_parse_uri_reply. Consequently, arbitrary DNS URI replies do not reach its URI-specific validation, record-list construction, string allocation/copying, TTL extraction, or error cleanup paths.
evidence: include/ares.h adds the public ares_parse_uri_reply API and struct ares_uri_reply.
ares_parse_uri_reply parses attacker-controlled abuf/alen, requires qdcount == 1, iterates ancount records, filters rr_class == C_IN and rr_type == T_URI, and handles variable rr_len.

For accepted URI records, ares_parse_uri_reply allocates ARES_DATATYPE_URI_REPLY nodes, links them through next, allocates uri using rr_len, copies record bytes, and invokes ares_free_data on failures.
ares_data.c adds URI-specific allocation initialization and recursive list/string cleanup under ARES_DATATYPE_URI_REPLY.

H0 calls ares_parse_a_reply, ares_parse_aaaa_reply, ares_parse_ptr_reply, ares_parse_ns_reply, ares_parse_srv_reply, ares_parse_mx_reply, ares_parse_txt_reply, ares_parse_soa_reply, ares_parse_naptr_reply, and ares_parse_caa_reply, but not ares_parse_uri_reply.
recommended_action: Extend H0 to call ares_parse_uri_reply(data, size, &uri), then free any returned list with ares_free_data(uri), so malformed, mixed-type, multi-answer, boundary-length, allocation, and cleanup behavior is fuzzed.
